versions.text: Criterion: Verify (if required for proper operation of ice protection equipment) that monitoring of icing conditions or incipient icing can be accomplished by the crew throughout the design envelope. Standard: No single environmental protection subsystem failure (including control station functions that are critical to air vehicle flight safety) results in flying qualities less than level three or loss of aircraft. Method of Compliance: The standard is verified by the following activities: a. Analysis and/or simulation determine the severity of the environment that drives protection needs for the air vehicle system. b. Capability analysis and test verify the adequacy of environmental protection system mechanisms required for air vehicle system safety of flight profile. c. FMECA and hazard analysis including the control station verifies that any failure of the environmental protection subsystem does not affect safety of flight operations. References: JSSG-2009: D.3.4.4.11, D.4.4.4.11 Ice protection 14 CFR 23.1419, 25.1419, 27.1419, 29.1419

Standard: A means exists of monitoring the flight environment for icing conditions (atmospheric conditions of visible moisture and temperature that are conducive to airframe and inlet icing) or incipient icing by the flight crew or an automated system throughout the air vehicle flight envelope. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review design documents to verify that methods of monitoring the flight environment for potential icing environments are provided. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct system-level testing in an environment laboratory to verify that flight environment monitoring provisions detect potential icing conditions prior to accumulation of ice on the air vehicle. Prior to entering operational test or operations, verify the standard by the following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct flight testing with a chase air vehicle to verify that flight environment monitoring provisions detect potential icing conditions prior to accumulation of ice on the air vehicle.
